pricing_formulas._note: T135+ REWRITTEN (PRICING_GUIDE section 4.2/10.2 P3, direct business input): replaces the prior flat_tier_price ($140) two-tier model, which had a confirmed, live bug (B3) -- the swap rate's own Tier 2 never activated below 96 units, so every real job from 1 to 95 units priced identically at $140 flat, regardless of actual size. New model: swap covers 20 units for a flat $20, then $1.00/unit; new_holes covers 10 units for a flat $35, then $3.50/unit -- continuous, no downward cliff, verified against the reference ladder (12 units swap=$20/new_holes=$42; 22 units swap=$22/new_holes=$77; 100 units swap=$100/new_holes=$350). T156 (operator ruling #112, option A, 2026-10-07): the old model above priced 1 to 20 swap knobs identically at $20, so a customer with ten knobs was quoted what a customer with one is. It is kept as the FLOOR: price = max(visit_minimum, tier total, the old flat price for the install type), so no job is quoted less than before. `tiers` are GRADUATED (marginal): the first 5 units are $20 each, units 6-15 are $15 each, every unit after the 15th is $10 (up_to_units is the cumulative count the tier runs to; null = open-ended). Graduated, not whole-order, because pricing the whole order at the tier its count falls in makes the price FALL as the count rises (5 knobs $100, 6 knobs $90; 15 knobs $225, 16 knobs $160), which the Charter forbids (quantity-per-unit labor scales continuously, never stepped). The tiers apply to both install types; new holes take longer (6 min per unit against 3) but the ruling set one table, so today they price the same. workflow._note: Phase 0 (Orchestrator Overhaul). This node is the active rulebook for routing, intake-question selection, confidence gating, and pricing -- not passive documentation. Every entry path (Catalog browse, Other-tile tap, free-text SmartQuote) must produce a BookingContext and pass it through executeWorkflow(context, db), which walks these steps in order. See Phase 5.5's _archaeology_notes on individual rules below for the specific real bug each rule exists to prevent -- these were extracted from actual hardcoded logic found and fixed during the architecture-audit sessions, not invented speculatively.

steps._note: Resolves BookingContext -> a concrete service or dynamic_service entity. For entry='catalog' or 'other_tile', selectedServiceId/selectedGroupId already pin this down directly. For entry='free_text', this step delegates to intent_mappings.objects keyword/synonym matching (NOT a hardcoded keyword map -- see the architecture-audit finding that resolveGroupFromIntent's hardcoded rules and intent_mappings.objects were two parallel, partially-overlapping systems; this workflow makes intent_mappings.objects the single real source going forward).

fallback._warn: no entity resolved with sufficient confidence

steps._note: Computes a small set of NAMED, independently-auditable booleans -- NOT a single opaque chainIsQtyOnly flag. Archaeology finding: the legacy chainIsQtyOnly check was too coarse to correctly handle behavior.bypass_intake services, 3 of which (high_ceiling_bulb_replacement, shower_head_replacement, tub_spout_replacement) have ONE real, price-affecting, non-quantity question that must still be asked even though the service is otherwise flagged for minimal friction. A single boolean cannot represent that distinction; named, separate flags can.

produces.chain_is_pure_quantity: true only if every module in the resolved intake_chain is a recognized quantity-style module (item_count, count, hybrid_qty, global_quantity)
produces.chain_is_single_simple_question: true if the chain has exactly one module AND that module is item_count_template (a banded quantity question) -- distinct from chain_is_pure_quantity, since item_count_template is NOT in the legacy quantity-module set but is still simple enough to bypass extensive intake when paired with behavior.bypass_intake
produces.chain_has_real_non_quantity_question: true if the chain contains any module that is neither a quantity-style module nor item_count_template -- when true, intake bypass rules MUST still surface that question; bypassing it would silently drop a real, price-affecting answer
produces.all_visible_real_questions_answered: true once every currently-visible (per _isModVisible) non-quantity module has a real answer in BookingContext.answers

steps._note: Builds the final, real list of intake questions to ask: entity.intake_chain (the named modules) + global_rules.intake_defaults (category_defaults/group_defaults/universal, scoped by category/group -- replaces the deprecated, unconditional global_rules.force_modules_by_variability_DEPRECATED as of T118) + then-branch targets unlocked by already-given answers. Archaeology finding: an earlier version of this logic (S._forceModules) was SET but never CONSUMED in the legacy curated-intake renderer -- confirmed and fixed mid-session; this step makes that consumption a mandatory, auditable part of the workflow rather than something that can silently regress again.

Archaeology finding (direct feedback during the session): the location chip/NLP-extracted location was being treated as cosmetic filler/notes despite carrying real, derivable intent (a 'front door' implies solid-core, a 'bedroom door' implies hollow-core; a 'toilet' near 'guest bedroom' is genuinely ambiguous and must NOT be guessed). This step pre-fills an intake answer ONLY when context.extractedLocation matches exactly one client_response[*].location_hints entry for a given module -- never when zero or multiple answers claim the same location, and never overriding an answer the user already gave.

Archaeology finding: the legacy curated-intake renderer used a hardcoded tagBonus (+5 skilled / +10 specialized, ADDED TO THE SCORE) instead of global_rules.confidence_escalation's real +15/+30 deltas (which RAISE THE BAR). These are mechanically different operations that were both firing in the same wrong direction -- confirmed via direct trace to make the Estimate button enable roughly 20 points too early for a real service (flatscreen_mounting_standard + #brick_wall: bar should rise 50->65, legacy code left it at 50 while also inflating the score). This step performs ONLY the bar-raising operation (confidence_escalation), and a separate, additive scoring step (base_confidence + module gains + NLP match confidence) computes the score independently -- the two must never be conflated into one number again.
See ui_template_matrix below -- this is the corrected version of Phase 3's example, using the named flags from compute_variability_flags instead of a single chainIsQtyOnly boolean.

Archaeology finding (post-session audit): 51 services have real services.*.required_materials and 35 have optional_materials, referencing real materials_catalog SKUs with real prices and a real markup_percent (confirmed uniformly 20% in global_rules.surcharges) -- NONE of which is read at runtime; every materials display reads the separate, often-stale default_estimates.materials.min/max instead (confirmed 3 real services, e.g. dishwasher_repair, where the legacy number and the catalog-derived number would genuinely differ). Resolution, NOT deletion (Chesterton's Fence: default_estimates.materials.note frequently carries real, business-meaningful customer-facing explanation -- e.g. dishwasher_repair's 'Exact part cost cannot be determined before diagnosis' -- that has no equivalent in the catalog data and must be preserved): when required_materials/optional_materials is non-empty, compute min = sum(required SKU prices * (1+markup)), max = min + sum(optional SKU prices * (1+markup)), and use this as the authoritative materials range -- but ALWAYS carry forward default_estimates.materials.note verbatim if present, regardless of which range won.

Invokes the SINGLE unified pricing function for every entry path -- no separate _computePrice. Archaeology finding: the legacy Catalog-browse path's _computePrice never included global_rules.surcharges.dispatch_fee at all, while the SmartQuote path's computeUnifiedQuote always did -- the exact same service could quote differently by the full dispatch fee ($45) depending on which UI entry point was tapped. Confirmed and fixed mid-session by adding the fee to _computePrice directly (a stopgap); this workflow's real fix is that _computePrice no longer exists as a separate function at all once Phase 6 lands -- every entry path reaches this exact step.

Equals service_types.Repair.base_price (70), the type a service with no declared type is priced as, so the same number is held twice (PENDING_DECISIONS #142).
_notes.tier_rate: Hourly rate (USD) used when the complexity tier a quote resolves to has no row in global_rules.complexity_tiers. Equals complexity_tiers.skilled.hourly_rate (85), the tier a service with no stated tier is priced as, so the same number is held twice (#142). _notes.dispatch_fee: Dispatch fee (USD, charged once per visit) used when surcharges.dispatch_fee is absent. Equals surcharges.dispatch_fee (45), so the same number is held twice (#142). The reader tests the field for truthiness, so an authored dispatch_fee of 0 is read as absent and this value is charged instead; to waive the fee author surcharges.dispatch_fee_enabled: false, which is the documented switch (#142).
_notes.standard_labor: Hourly labor rate (USD) of the furniture-assembly minutes calculation, which also sets its one-hour minimum charge, used when meta.global_rates.standard_labor is absent. Equals meta.global_rates.standard_labor (40), so the same number is held twice (#142).
_notes.default_minutes: Minutes the Buy-the-Hour floor assumes ONE JOB takes (the work the service's base price pays for: the '1 item' case) when the service authors neither a minutes range (default_estimates.total_minutes) nor operational_metrics.expected_minutes. It is a per-JOB duration, one line of the cart, and not a per-visit figure: a visit has no minutes of its own, only the dispatch fee. Its one reader is the buy_the_hour_qty_gate_formula in applyPricingFormula: for an order of more than one item the formula tops the job up to the billing minimum, extraMin = max(0, minimum_billable_hours x 60 - this value). At 60 that is minimum_billable_hours (1) x 60, so the top-up is 0 and the order bills exactly one hour at the service's own rate. The two numbers are independent: raising minimum_billable_hours without raising this one adds the difference as billable minutes. The pricing-archetype path calls the formula without the service, so on that path this value is always the one used. The same question, how long is a job nobody estimated, is answered 45 (no_estimate_minutes), 30 (the archetype calculator) and 45 or 60 (cart lines) elsewhere in the code; PENDING_DECISIONS #143 asks for one answer. Until it is ruled this stays at 60 and no price moves.

Read by computeUnifiedQuote and by the formula branch of computeArchetypeQuote. It is the same question as default_minutes, answered differently (45 here, 60 there); the two were kept apart by history and not by meaning, and PENDING_DECISIONS #143 asks for one answer. Until it is ruled this stays at 45 and no price moves.

charter.note: The vocabulary of the three independent axes (skill tier, risk tier, batch-risk flag). Every term is the Charter's own; a hazard or basis a service cites must be named here, so the choice of each value can be reviewed against the meaning. A service's profile is the floor of its typical resolved shape: an answer, a tag or a branch promotes it as the job reveals itself (P-COMPLEX-DYNAMIC). The risk tier is the highest tier among the hazards a service names; the batch flag is true exactly when it names a ground. No axis is derived from another.
charter.decided_under: G-GOVERN-AUTONOMY (T180): the values were derived from the Charter's definitions and each service's authored record, not asserted; PENDING_DECISIONS.md lists what an Operator may overrule.

none.meaning: R0: no hazard, no shutoff, no permit, no regulation.

minor_water.meaning: R1: minor water. Work at a fixture downstream of its own working stop valve; a failure leaks at the fixture and is contained.

minor_electrical.meaning: R1: minor electrical. Work at a lamp socket or bulb, or on low-voltage control wiring; no fixed branch-circuit wiring is opened. Plugging a device into an outlet is not a hazard.

ladder_under_16ft.meaning: R1: ladder work with the working height under sixteen feet.

weight_to_50lb.meaning: R1: handles weights up to fifty pounds.

dust_debris.meaning: R1: dust and debris, but no structural involvement.

active_water.meaning: R2: active water. Replaces or alters a stop valve, a supply line or a sealed supply or drain connection; a failure leaks under line pressure or into the structure.

active_electrical.meaning: R2: active electrical. Opens or connects fixed branch-circuit wiring (an outlet, a switch, a fixture, a fan) or the inside of a mains-powered appliance.

active_gas.meaning: R2: active gas. Work on, or on the connection of, a gas appliance.

structural.meaning: R2: structural condition. The work meets, or may reveal, a condition in framing, subfloor, masonry or a crack that can signal movement.

permit_or_code.meaning: R2: a permit is required or a code applies to the work.

height_over_16ft.meaning: R2: working height over sixteen feet.

weight_over_50lb.meaning: R2: handles weights over fifty pounds.

batch_physical_bases.drilled_hole: A drilled hole: one bad hole among many is a door, a wall or a cabinet that needs replacing (R-COMPLEX-AXES).
batch_physical_bases.cut: A cut: a mis-cut length or opening cannot be un-cut.
batch_physical_bases.sealed_joint: A sealed joint whose seal is made once (a compression ferrule, a wax seal, a solvent weld): a bad one is redone by replacing the part.
batch_physical_bases.adhered_surface: An adhered surface: an adhesive, a compound or a patch that cannot be lifted and reapplied.
batch_physical_bases.mis_sized_order: A mis-sized order: the part is made to fit one opening and fits no other.

batch_signals.overflow_formula: The service's pricing formula declares an overflow rate (R-COMPLEX-COMPOUNDS: each unit past the included count is nearly a full job).
batch_signals.per_unit_penalty_minutes: The service's pricing formula declares penalty minutes (R-COMPLEX-COMPOUNDS: its author believed the N-th unit carries non-linear risk).
batch_signals.single_use_consumable: The service's required materials include a single-use consumable listed in single_use_consumable_material_ids (R-COMPLEX-COMPOUNDS: one mistake wastes a consumable that cannot be reused). Written as single_use_consumable:<material id>.
batch_signals.scope_changing_branch: An answer in the service's intake routes to another service (R-COMPLEX-COMPOUNDS: the batch has heterogeneous instances, and one of them can promote the whole job).

A0.meaning: Simple: identical SKU within the authored per-item, total-duration and quantity limits; no wall anchoring, electrical work, cutting, two-person lift or site modification.

A1.meaning: Standard flat-pack: mixed SKUs, a duration or quantity beyond the A0 limits, or one mild complication.

A2.meaning: Complex: configurable or large assembly, wall anchoring, a required two-person lift, or work beyond the authored standard limits.

A3.meaning: Custom or built-in: site measurement, cutting, electrical integration, structural involvement, a permit, or a multi-visit project.

The service's own name, its description's words, and 'ram' / 'memory upgrade' are synonyms here, at full weight.
nlp_objects._note_t170: T170 (#180): 'power supply' and 'psu' are the name of a part the Computer Repair part service now offers (computer_component 'Power supply (desktop)'); without them 'my psu is dead' and 'install a power supply' matched nothing and fell to a wall-mounting question. Full weight, like 'ram' and 'ssd': a distinct word from this entry's keyword, so at half weight it missed the 50-point gate. 'new power supply for my desktop' still names a computer, which is a stronger object (85); the service's description decides that sibling (see the descriptions of computer_diagnostic and internal_hardware_replacement).

nlp_objects._note_new_keyword: v9.6 NEW SERVICE (working design, per explicit instruction to build this out with best judgment -- clearly marked as such, needs business validation): weight 70, deliberately just above the existing 'tile' keyword's own 65 -- confirmed directly this is sufficient for this entry to always win outright over the generic tile match whenever 'ceiling' is present (detectIntentNLP keeps only the single highest-scoring entry). This is the real, structural fix for the routing gap found in T96 -- 'ceiling tile'/'drop ceiling' now resolves to its own real group (minor_home_repairs_ceilings) instead of silently matching the wall/floor tile intent. Real, genuine synonyms given full weight (not the generic half-weight) since each is exactly as specific and unambiguous as the primary keyword itself, same reasoning already established for other entries' full_weight_synonyms.

nlp_default_fallback._note_authoring: v9.6: removed dangling service_id ('generic_handyman_service', confirmed never existed as a real catalog service, and confirmed via workflow's own archaeology note never actually read by any code even when it did resolve). The remaining fields (category/service_type/base_price) already, correctly describe this as a category-level fallback -- workflow.fallback_routing_rules routes on category+service_type alone when nothing more specific resolves, needing no specific named service_id at all. Leaving a dangling reference was strictly worse than omitting the field: any future code that starts reading it would hit a real, broken lookup rather than correctly falling through to the generic_wizard path this fallback already, properly routes to.
